q.intro.text: Forty seventh graders each picked one lunch. Ten of them picked pizza. You draw a circle graph of all forty answers. How big is the angle of the pizza slice? Pick an answer, and say how sure you are.

e.intro.text: Let's work it out in four steps. Press each one, and watch the picture first, then the maths on the board.

e.step0.text: The whole circle is all forty students. That's one hundred percent of them, and a full turn of three hundred sixty degrees. Each dot is one student.

e.step1.text: Ten of the forty picked pizza. Ten fortieths is one fourth of the whole.

e.step2.text: One fourth of one hundred percent is twenty-five percent. And one fourth of three hundred sixty degrees is ninety degrees: a quarter turn.

e.step3.text: Tacos, salad and pasta go around the same way, each slice starting where the last one ended. The angles close the circle at three hundred sixty degrees. Each label gets the name and the percent, and the title names the whole.

e.why.text: Quick check. Why is the pizza angle ninety degrees, and not twenty-five?

e.why.ok.text: Yes. The share is the same on both scales. One fourth of one hundred percent is twenty-five percent, and one fourth of three hundred sixty degrees is ninety degrees.

e.why.pctdeg.text: That mixes up the two scales. Twenty-five is out of one hundred, but the circle is three hundred sixty degrees, so a quarter of it is ninety degrees.

e.why.half.text: A full turn is three hundred sixty degrees, not one hundred eighty. One hundred eighty degrees is only half the circle.

t.intro.text: Now sixty students picked their favorite sport. I'll do the first two steps. Then it's your turn.

t.given.text: The whole is sixty students: one hundred percent, three hundred sixty degrees. Soccer is twenty-one of them: twenty-one sixtieths.

t.pct.text: What percent of the sixty students picked soccer?

t.pct.ok.text: Right. Twenty-one sixtieths of one hundred percent is thirty-five percent.

t.pct.fixed.text: Twenty-one is the count, not the percent. The whole is sixty students, not one hundred. Take twenty-one sixtieths of one hundred percent.

t.pct.noscale.text: Zero point three five is the share as a decimal. A percent is per hundred: multiply it by one hundred.

t.pct.miss.text: Take twenty-one sixtieths of one hundred percent. Try again.

t.deg.text: Now the angle. How many degrees is the soccer slice?

t.deg.ok.text: Right. Twenty-one sixtieths of three hundred sixty degrees is one hundred twenty-six degrees. Watch it sweep.

t.deg.pctdeg.text: Thirty-five is the percent. The circle is three hundred sixty degrees, not one hundred. Take twenty-one sixtieths of three hundred sixty degrees.

t.deg.half.text: That uses one hundred eighty degrees for the whole circle. A full turn is three hundred sixty degrees.

t.deg.times.text: That's twenty-one times three hundred sixty degrees: twenty-one whole circles. Take twenty-one sixtieths of three hundred sixty degrees.

t.deg.miss.text: Take twenty-one sixtieths of three hundred sixty degrees. Try again.

t.next.text: Basketball is next: ninety degrees. Where does its slice start?

t.next.ok.text: Yes. At one hundred twenty-six degrees, where soccer ends. Every slice starts at the last slice's edge.

t.next.no.text: From the top again, basketball would lie on top of soccer. It starts where soccer ends, at one hundred twenty-six degrees.

t.label.text: Last step. Which label goes on the soccer slice?

t.label.ok.text: Yes. The name and the percent. The degrees are only for drawing.

t.label.deg.text: One hundred twenty-six degrees is what you drew with the protractor. A reader wants the share: thirty-five percent.

t.label.count.text: Twenty-one is the count. The label shows the percent of the whole: thirty-five percent.

t.done.text: Back to the pizza question. Ten fortieths is one fourth of the circle, and one fourth of three hundred sixty degrees is ninety degrees.

p.intro.text: Riley made a circle graph of the lunch survey, and says: my percents add up to one hundred percent, and my angles add up to three hundred sixty degrees, so my graph is right. Is Riley right?

p.build.no.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.build.yes.text: Let's test it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true, and see where it leads.

p.c1.text: Tacos is fourteen of forty students. That's thirty-five percent of the circle, so a slice of one hundred twenty-six degrees. That's the dashed outline.

p.c2.text: But the slice with Riley's tacos label has a right angle. It's only ninety degrees, a quarter.

p.c3.text: Riley swapped the pizza and tacos labels. Swapping two labels changes no total, so the totals could not catch it.

p.done.text: That's a proof. Three claims, each with its reason, and the picture backs every one. Right totals are needed, but they are not enough.

p.chip.total.text: That is exactly Riley's mistake. The totals can be right while a slice is wrong.

p.chip.pctdeg.text: Careful. Twenty-five percent of the circle is a ninety degree angle, not twenty-five degrees.

p.chip.radius.text: The size of the circle changes nothing. A slice's share is set by its angle.

p.chip.other.text: True, but it's the reason for a different line. Which one makes this line true?
